reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a Chipotle eating show in which the presenter consumes food and invites ordinary audience engagement through liking and subscribing. The described referral links offer shopping discounts or creator rewards tied to purchases or sign-up activity, without establishing a deceptive mechanism or connecting them to the mukbang content.

citations.quote: Chipotle Mexican Grill | MUKBANG (Eating Show)
So, uh, I picked up some Chipotle.
Make an order using my referral link of $15 or more at Paula's Choice and you'll get $10 off of your purchase

opening.argument: The video description explicitly links viewer purchasing or signing up through external referral links to financial benefits for the creator. It asks viewers to make a purchase of at least $15 through one link, promising the viewer a discount while also awarding the creator money toward a future purchase; another link gives the viewer points and the creator even more points. That is a direct action-to-reward solicitation, not merely casual lifestyle discussion. The presentation of ordinary personal content gives these requests a familiar, trusted setting, while the repeated external links create the participation pathway. On that evidence, the central concern is a referral-based commission structure whose commercial incentive is easy to overlook.

citations.quote: Make an order using my referral link of $15 or more at Paula's Choice and you'll get $10 off of your purchase
If you're thinking about purchasing anything online, then I'd highly suggest you do so through Ebates!
you'll receive 5 points (redeemable for gift cards to Amazon & Sephora) and I'll receive 10 points

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the links “shopping discounts” does not remove the commission mechanism. The description expressly says the creator receives money, points, or future purchasing credit when viewers act. The fact that the meal itself is ordinary does not answer whether the embedded calls to purchase and sign up constitute a recruitment-based referral solicitation.

citations.quote: as well as earn me $10 towards a future Paula's Choice purchase
I'll receive 10 points

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited language shows disclosed, one-level referral benefits, but it does not show downlines, team structures, matrices, tier qualification, or income dependent on recruiting participants. A discount for a buyer and points for a creator are ordinary referral incentives, not evidence of a recruitment commission scheme. The links also do not establish deception or a false promised return.

citations.quote: Paula's Choice Referral Link (only works for new customers, sorry!!)
I'll receive 10 points

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: multiple external referral links, shortened URLs, creator-specific rewards, and incentives redeemable for gift cards. The description encourages viewers to route online purchases through a referral link, offers a discount conditional on a minimum order, and separately promises points to both the new registrant and the creator. These are not passive mentions; they are several participation funnels attached to financial or gift-card benefits. The disclaimer that the links are not affiliate links does not erase the disclosed fact that the creator receives money, points, or purchasing credit when viewers act. A careful review should therefore treat the lifestyle setting as a vehicle for referral promotion and classify the content under recruitment-linked commissions.

citations.quote: If you're thinking about purchasing anything online, then I'd highly suggest you do so through Ebates!
you'll get $10 off of your purchase (as well as earn me $10 towards a future Paula's Choice purchase)!
you'll receive 5 points (redeemable for gift cards to Amazon & Sephora) and I'll receive 10 points
The above links are not affiliate links

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense isolates the meal and treats each incentive as harmless, but it does not explain the combination of multiple external funnels, minimum-purchase conditions, and creator rewards redeemable for purchases or gift cards. The disclaimer is itself an admission that the links and compensation issue require attention; it is not proof that the solicitation is non-deceptive.

citations.quote: Make an order using my referral link of $15 or more
redeemable for gift cards to Amazon & Sephora

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are disclosed incentives, not hidden or unusually large returns. The evidence identifies ordinary purchases, a new-customer discount, and points, but no promise of income, no deposit or withdrawal process, and no multi-level structure. Shortened URLs and several links may warrant scrutiny, yet they do not establish that viewers are deceived or recruited into a tiered commission system.

citations.quote: only works for new customers, sorry!!
The above links are not affiliate links; some have just been shortened with tiny url to make this description box less messy.

opening.argument: Although the video is framed as an eating show, its surrounding presentation also functions as promotion. The creator turns a personal audience relationship into repeated invitations to follow external links, make purchases, register for a creator program, and subscribe for future content. The description places these commercial pathways alongside personal details and social handles, making the solicitation feel like part of an intimate lifestyle recommendation rather than a separate advertisement. The referral program is especially significant because the viewer's participation produces a benefit for the creator: purchases generate money or future credit, and registration generates points. The apparent entertainment framing therefore does not prevent the content from operating as a recruitment-oriented referral promotion.

citations.quote: Chipotle Mexican Grill | MUKBANG (Eating Show)
If you're thinking about purchasing anything online, then I'd highly suggest you do so through Ebates!
Make an order using my referral link of $15 or more at Paula's Choice and you'll get $10 off of your purchase
If you did, please. Do go ahead and give me a thumbs up down below.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The eating-show title describes the surface format, not the full commercial function of the upload. The defense acknowledges referral links but calls them disconnected from the content; however, they are presented in the same creator-controlled description that asks viewers to engage, purchase, and sign up. The ordinary meal can increase trust in those recommendations rather than disprove their promotional role.

citations.quote: SO MUCH INFO BELOW
P.O. BOX

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The video visibly and verbally centers on eating Chipotle: the title calls it an eating show, and the presenter says she picked up Chipotle. A description containing social links and disclosed referral offers does not transform the main entertainment into a recruitment scheme. The evidence still lacks tiers, downlines, required participation, or a deceptive promise of earnings.
